transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I called the EAP because lately every little bang at work makes me jump really hard—like a file drawer slamming or someone dropping a coffee mug. My chest starts racing, and it takes way longer than it should to calm back down.
Have you been avoiding any places or situations because of these reactions?
I don’t think so. I mean, I still go to work and do the normal stuff. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding any particular place or situation.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge when there aren't any loud noises or surprises happening?

Yeah, I think so. Even when nothing is happening, I’m kind of on alert in the office. I keep checking where my boss is, where the exits are, and if someone’s coming up behind me, even when I’m supposed to be focused on my team.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently or in the past?
I’m not really sure. Nothing that I can point to as, like, a major traumatic event. It’s more that these reactions started happening, but I don’t know what set them off.
Do you have any recurring memories, thoughts, or images that disturb you or are hard to shake?
Not really. I mean, I don’t have a specific memory or image that keeps coming back or anything like that. It’s more just a general uneasy feeling, but I can’t point to a recurring thought.
Do you often find yourself worrying about everyday things, like work, finances, or relationships, even when there's no obvious reason to worry?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about work sometimes like anyone, but it doesn’t feel like I’m constantly worrying about money or relationships for no reason. That’s not really what I’ve noticed.
Do you find that you're often preoccupied with worries about things that might go wrong in the future?

No, I don’t think that’s really it. I’m not usually sitting around thinking about all the things that could go wrong. I mean, I have normal concerns, but I wouldn’t say I’m preoccupied with future worries.
Do you feel like you're worrying more days than not over the past few months?
No, I wouldn’t say that. I haven’t noticed myself worrying most days for months or anything like that. It’s not really been a constant thing.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes and included symptoms like a racing heart or shortness of breath?

No, I don’t think I’ve had that. I mean, I’ve felt stressed or uncomfortable before, but not like a sudden rush of intense fear that peaks in a few minutes with my heart racing or not being able to breathe.
Do you feel anxious or fearful in situations where most people would not, such as in a crowded store or while driving?
No, not really. Crowded stores or driving don’t usually make me anxious like that. I haven’t noticed being scared in situations where other people seem fine.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's nothing in particular to worry about?
Not really. I mean, I get concerned if there’s something actually going on, but I don’t usually find myself worrying for no reason.
Do you feel like you're more anxious than other people in everyday situations that wouldn't normally cause anxiety?
No, I wouldn’t say that. Day to day, I don’t think I’m more anxious than other people in normal situations.
Do you usually expect the worst to happen even when things are going well?
No, I don’t think so. If things are going okay, I usually take it that way. I’m not sitting there expecting everything to fall apart.
Do you often find yourself having trouble controlling your worry?
No, not really. If I’m worried about something specific, I can usually settle down once I think it through or deal with it. It doesn’t feel out of my control most of the time.
Do you feel nervous or uneasy in everyday situations, like when you're at home or with friends, even when everything seems to be going fine?
No, I haven’t really noticed that. If I’m at home or with friends and things are fine, I’m usually okay.
Do you often feel like something is going to go wrong, even when things are calm?
No, I wouldn’t say that’s something I often feel. When things are calm, I can usually recognize that and not assume something bad is about to happen.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things for more than a few days at a time?
Not usually, no. I might worry about something for a bit if there’s a reason, but it doesn’t normally stick around for days and days.
Do you often feel like you're worrying about things for no reason at all?
Not really. I mean, I worry when there’s something actually going on, but I don’t usually feel like I’m worrying for no reason.
Do you feel like your anxiety is out of proportion to the actual danger or threat in a situation?

Yeah… I think so, at least sometimes. Like when I’m in the office, I catch myself constantly checking where my boss is, where the exits are, and if anyone’s coming up behind me. There’s usually no real reason for it, and I’m supposed to be focused on my team, but I still keep scanning around.
Do you feel anxious or on edge most of the time, regardless of what you're doing or where you are?

Not most of the time, no. It’s more when I’m at the office. I’ll catch myself checking where my boss is, where the exits are, and whether someone’s coming up behind me, even when I’m supposed to be focused on my team.
